description: COVID-19 Scenarios is a browser-based tool that models outbreak trajectories and hospital demand for a chosen region under different mitigation scenarios. The user selects or enters a population with its age distribution, the number of hospital and ICU beds, epidemiological parameters and a timeline of interventions, and the model projects infections, hospital and ICU occupancy against available capacity, and fatalities by age group. The Neher Lab at the Biozentrum of the University of Basel built it in 2020 so that health planners and the public could explore how interventions change the burden on hospitals. Coverage: preset scenarios for many countries and regions, and any region the user defines; resolution is one region, age bands and days. It runs entirely in the web browser at covid19-scenarios.org, and the TypeScript and JavaScript source is on GitHub (latest tag 1.12.0). Licence: MIT, free, no registration. Caveats: parameters and presets date from 2020 and 2021, the project is no longer actively developed, and it is a compartmental model, not agent-based. Simulation uses: capacity planning of hospital and intensive-care beds and emergency response planning for pandemics. Related: CHIME is a simpler hospital impact model and Covasim an agent-based alternative (catalogued as model-chime and model-covasim).
